newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea replaces investigator in bribery scandal.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea replaces investigator in bribery scandal.

text.p: South Korea's top investigator into a bribery scandal involving loans to failed Hanbo Steel Co was replaced on Friday, a Justice Ministry statement said.

Opposition parties have blasted as a whitewash a state prosecution probe led by Choi Byung-koog into Hanbo Steel that has led to the trial of 10 people, including a former cabinet minister. The opposition says the main culprits have escaped justice.
"Some misunderstandings have occurred during the Hanbo investigation," the statement said. "The replacement was made to ensure a transparent and fair investigation to reveal the truth."
Hanbo Steel collapsed in January under $5.8 million in improper loans.
Former cabinet minister Kim Woo-suk, close aides to President Kim Young-sam, Hanbo founder Chung Tae-soo and his chief accountant as well as three top bankers are standing trial on bribery charges.
Parliament on Friday launched a special probe into the scandal during which it will question the second son of President Kim Young-sam.
